The New York Times on Instagram: "A NASA rocket blasted off from Florida on Wednesday evening, lifting four astronauts toward space. Crowds cheered when the powerful vehicle launched into the clear, twilight sky at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time. It traveled eastward, over the Atlantic Ocean, on a journey that is to go around the moon but not land there.

The flight, aboard a spacecraft named Integrity, is expected to be a round trip of more than 695,000 miles to clear a path for more exploration, and eventually a new lunar landing. The mission, known as Artemis II, is the 21st century equivalent of Apollo 8, when NASA astronauts captured the rapt attention of the world.

Tap the link in our bio to read the latest updates on NASA’s Artemis II mission and its 10-day lunar journey. Photos by @kenny_holston and @cassandraklos_"
